summary: Implemented Docker availability detection and read-only container listing. The remote script always exits 0 when Docker isn't installed (reported via a PIHUB_DOCKER_AVAILABLE marker, never a command failure); when Docker is available, docker ps's own exit code/stderr propagate naturally, which required enriching SshError::RemoteCommandError with stderr so a permission-denied failure can be distinguished from any other command error. Both Unavailable and PermissionDenied are normal Ok outcomes at the collect_docker_containers layer, never surfaced as SshError. 17 new Rust unit tests, 99 total passing.
completed: infrastructure/ssh/operation.rs: DOCKER_CONTAINERS_COMMAND -- checks `command -v docker`, prints PIHUB_DOCKER_AVAILABLE=0/1, then runs `docker ps -a --no-trunc --format '{{json .}}'` as the script's final command so its exit status/stderr propagate through the existing error path.
infrastructure/ssh/error.rs: enriched SshError::RemoteCommandError with stderr (was exit_code only); updated Display impl and existing WU007 tests.

infrastructure/parsers/docker.rs: parse_docker_containers() parses docker ps JSON lines independently (malformed lines warn and are skipped, valid ones kept); state strings map to DockerContainerState with unrecognized -> Unknown; health is derived from the Status text since docker ps has no dedicated health field; ports parsed from Docker's host->container/protocol string format, tolerating unpublished ports and multiple bindings.
collect_docker_containers(): runs the fixed operation and classifies into DockerCollectionResult::{Available, Unavailable, PermissionDenied} -- the latter two are normal Ok outcomes, never SshError.
Marked the new domain/parser code #[allow(dead_code)] since nothing calls it yet -- the M3 scheduler wires it up -- following the WU007/WU009 precedent.

17 new Rust unit tests: well-formed/malformed/empty docker ps payloads, port parsing edge cases, health/state derivation, the availability marker, and collect_docker_containers integration via FakeRemoteExecutor across all five outcome types.
Verified cargo test (99/99), cargo build (no warnings), and npm run build all pass.
Syntax-checked the remote script with both `sh -n` and `dash -n`.

validationCommands.summary: Unaffected by this backend-only work unit; still succeeds.

validationCommands.command: manual: sh -n and dash -n against the remote script
validationCommands.summary: Both shells accept the script's syntax.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: A device with Docker unavailable still reports online with valid system metrics
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: DockerCollectionResult::Unavailable is a normal Ok return from collect_docker_containers, never an error; collect_reports_unavailable_when_docker_is_not_installed test. System metrics collection (WU009) is entirely independent of Docker collection, so nothing here can fail it.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: A Docker permission error is classified as DockerPermissionError and does not fail the whole device refresh
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: collect_classifies_permission_denied_without_failing test: a RemoteCommandError with 'permission denied' in stderr maps to Ok(DockerCollectionResult::PermissionDenied), not an Err that would propagate as a device-level failure.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Rust unit tests cover well-formed, malformed, and empty docker ps output

notes: Risk score: 25/100 (low-medium). Rationale: same profile as WU009 -- the parsing/classification logic is thoroughly unit-tested and purely data-in/data-out, but the remote shell script has only been syntax-checked, not run against a real Raspberry Pi with Docker installed. Recommend validating DOCKER_CONTAINERS_COMMAND against the real Pi 5 (which runs the Personal Finance containers) before relying on it, particularly the permission-denied stderr text match, which depends on the exact Docker CLI version's error message wording.

Enriching SshError::RemoteCommandError with stderr is a small but real change to WU007's public error type; all existing call sites and tests were updated and still pass, and the change makes the error generally more useful (any future remote command failure now carries diagnostic text, not just an exit code).

The MVP Docker scope explicitly excludes start/stop/restart/exec (spec section 13.4); nothing in this work unit adds any such capability -- the frontend has no path to construct anything beyond the fixed DockerContainers listing operation.
